pl-microsorum-pteropus.title: Java Fern
pl-microsorum-pteropus.summary: One of the easiest aquarium plants. You tie it onto driftwood or rock, and it grows in low light.
rows: Fully aquatic (it also grows above water in a humid paludarium)
Rhizome plant, grown attached to wood or rock
Attached to driftwood or rock, in the midground or background
None in the substrate. Its roots grip wood or rock, and it stays where you put it. Never bury the rhizome (the thick horizontal stem) or it will rot
From the water. It doesn't need fertilizer or CO2, but nutrients, CO2 and some water movement help it grow better
Split the rhizome, or grow on the baby plants that form on older leaves
notes: Tie or glue it to wood or rock. The roots take hold in a few months.
Dark spots under the leaves are spore patches, not disease.
Plant-eating fish mostly leave it alone. Scale & Stem lists it as goldfish-proof.

pl-cryptocoryne-wendtii-brown.title: Crypt Wendtii 'Brown' (Bronze)
pl-cryptocoryne-wendtii-brown.summary: A tough, compact crypt with wavy bronze-brown leaves. It does well in hard water, even in cichlid tanks.
rows: Low to high. The leaves turn their deepest brown in good light
Optional (Dennerle suggests 10–20 mg/L for best growth)
10–20 cm (4–8 in), sometimes up to 30 cm (12 in)
Moderate. It's a root feeder that spreads by runners into dense clumps, and can fill a 20–30 cm (8–12 in) patch in a few months. It doesn't like being moved once it's settled
Root feeder. Use root tabs or a nutrient-rich substrate for the best color and growth
Runners (daughter plants pop up around the parent)
notes: 'Crypt melt' is normal. Leaves may die back after planting or moving, and they usually regrow within 2–4 weeks. Don't pull the plant out.

sources.name: Tropica Aquarium Plants – Nutrition Capsules (root-zone feeding)

pl-anubias-barteri-nana.title: Anubias Nana
pl-anubias-barteri-nana.summary: A small, slow, very hardy plant with tough dark-green leaves. It grows on wood or rock and thrives in shade.
rows: Rhizome plant, grown attached to wood or rock
Foreground or midground. Attach to wood or rock, good for nano tanks
Low. It thrives in shady spots where other plants struggle
5–10 cm (2–4 in) tall, 5–20 cm (2–8 in) wide
None in the substrate. It grips wood or rock and doesn't spread on its own. Never bury the rhizome or it will rot
Cut the rhizome into pieces with a few leaves each
notes: Plant-eating fish don't eat it.
The leaves live for years, so slow algae can settle on them under strong light. A shadier spot helps.
It often flowers underwater.

pl-sagittaria-subulata.title: Dwarf Sagittaria
pl-sagittaria-subulata.summary: A grass-like foreground plant that spreads by runners into a carpet, even without CO2.
rows: Fully aquatic (it also grows in ponds and tolerates slightly brackish water)
Foreground (it can get tall, see below)
Low to medium. Strong light keeps it shorter
Not required, but CO2 speeds it up a lot
5–30 cm (2–12 in). Dense or older groups can grow up to 50–60 cm (20–24 in)
Aggressive spreader. Runners send up new plants every few days in good conditions and quickly form a dense mat. Plant pieces 2–4 cm (1–1.5 in) apart and thin the runners to keep it where you want it
Both roots and water. It's prone to iron shortage (yellowing leaves), so a nutrient-rich substrate or fertilizer helps
notes: It sometimes sends a flower stalk to the surface with small white flowers.
